The treaty promises $10 a person each year, rising to $15 once the nations settle on the reservation, for forty years. It names no total.
The price is $1 an acre for about 157,000 acres, with the nation’s debts and claims paid in addition.
Counts the sums promised to the Seneca and Shawnee. The Quapaw, Peoria and other nations party to the treaty were paid by the acre or from their own invested funds.
The treaty also allows up to $30,000 a year for food until the Ute can support themselves.
The treaty also promises clothing and $10 a year for each person who hunts and $20 for each who farms, for thirty years.
